chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنِ بَحْرٍ، كَوْفِيٌّ. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ، وَالرِّجَالِ. ضَعِيفٌ، مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ.

translations.en: ʿAbdullāh b. Baḥr, Kufan. Narrated from Abū Baṣīr, and the rijāl. Weak, a proponent of irtifāʿ in doctrine.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* identifies ʿAbdullāh ibn Baḥr as a Kufan narrator who transmitted from the prominent companion Abū Baṣīr al-Asadī. He is classified as weak (ḍaʿīf) with a 'raised' or elevated status in criticism, specifically noted for his adherence to irtifāʿ (elevation), a theological stance often linked to the Muʿtazilah or specific Shia debates regarding the exalted status of the Imams relative to prophets or other figures.
en.seo_question: Who is ʿAbdullāh ibn Baḥr and what is his status as a narrator in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.عبد الله بن بحر: ʿAbdullāh ibn Baḥr, the narrator being described
key_terms.كوفي: Kufan, indicating his origin from Kufa
key_terms.أبو بصير: Abū Baṣīr, a prominent companion of the Imams from whom he narrated
key_terms.ضعيف: Weak, a technical term in ʿIlm al-Rijāl indicating a narrator whose reliability is not sufficient for establishing independent legal rulings
key_terms.مرتفع القول: A proponent of irtifāʿ (exaltation/elevation) in doctrine, referring to a theological stance often linked to the Muʿtazilah or specific Shia theological schools regarding the status of the Imams
